event: Her last memory is being Alan, dozing over a book at his back window in the evening.
She sits up and long dark red hair falls over her shoulders and into her lap.
Her hands are small and pale, freckled across the backs, the nails short.
She finds a washstand with a small mirror: a freckled girl of about twenty, blue-grey eyes.
Under her nightshirt she has small soft breasts with pale pink nipples, and no cock at all.

event: She touches her face, her hair, her flat belly; every sense in this body is new to her.
The room: a bed, a washstand, a chest, a row of pegs, a window over grey slate rooftops.
Below the window, steep stone streets climb a mountainside, snow still on the peaks above.
Nala sees bare chimneys and a whole town glowing faintly orange in the dawn.
On a peg hangs a canvas pack with NALA stitched inside its flap.
In it: plain clothes, a knife, a coil of rope, a tin lamp.
She finds a letter asking the Delvers' Guild to register Nala Marsh of Fennick as a delver.
The letter is signed by the reeve of Fennick, a village three days down the valley.
She finds a thin purse: one silver coin and nine copper ones. She does not know what they buy.
She finds an iron key on a leather tag burned with the number 7.
Her memories are all Alan's; this Nala's life is a blank to her.
She wonders whether she can go back, and the room is silent on it.
She dresses clumsily in the clothes from the pack: shirt, laced bodice, breeches, boots.
She steps out onto a small top landing: one other door, marked 8, and a washroom.
Door 8 bangs open and a small sun-browned girl hops out, pulling on a boot.

event: The widow tells Nala her room is paid to the end of the week, and rent is taken on Restday.
Wren explains the stove: ember-stones from the Deep, warm and lit for months, no smoke.
Nala asks what the Deep is, and Wren stares, then laughs and tells her.
The Deep is a dungeon under the mountain with no bottom anyone has found; delvers go down it.
Wren says she has delved two years, holds iron rank, and opens most locks with a bent pin.
Wren mentions her party broke up in the winter and she is looking for another.
Wren offers to walk Nala down to the guild hall, since it is on her way to the party board.
They go down Ladder Lane, long flights of stone steps lined with rooming houses.
Nala's legs are shorter than she is used to, and she has to hurry to keep up.
Wren talks the whole way: coin is pennies, marks and crowns; twelve pennies to a mark.

event: At the bottom opens Coppergate, a square under a huge arched cave mouth in the mountain.
Wren names it the Mouth: the way into the Deep.
Beside the Mouth stands a house whose lamps are lit though it is morning: the Lantern House.

event: She is Elowen Fairweather, from Hollin Wood, and she reached Emberdeep only last night.
Elowen admits she is terrified; Nala admits she has no idea what she is doing either.
The clerk calls Elowen forward; she pays a silver mark and hands over her letter.
Elowen is given a copper token stamped with her name on a leather cord.
Nala goes up, hands over her letter, and pays her one silver mark.
The clerk reads the letter, writes Nala Marsh of Fennick in a ledger and moves straight on.
The clerk stamps a copper token NALA MARSH and hands it over on its cord.
Nala hangs the token round her neck; it is cold, then warm against her skin.
The clerk seats the morning's new delvers on a bench and reads the Rules of the Deep aloud.
Ranks run copper, iron, silver and gold; every new delver starts at copper.
A copper delver may go only to the first three levels, and only in a party of three or more.
The upper levels are mapped; the deeper ones far less; the passages shift by season.
Elowen whispers that she has no party; Nala whispers that neither does she.
At the party board, Nala sees Wren's name chalked among delvers looking for a party.
Nala buys a copy of the first level's map from the clerk for two pennies.
Elowen and Nala leave together, both a little stunned to be delvers.
Elowen asks if Nala minds her company for the morning, and Nala says she would like it.
They walk the finds market: lamps, rope, odd stones, bits of old metal, ember-stones by weight.
Nala holds an ember-stone at a stall; it is warm as a cup of tea, and glows soft orange.
Elowen tells her she is a hedge-witch's daughter, and knows herbs and simples.
In a quiet corner Elowen shows her shy trick: a small light called to her fingertips.
Nala is delighted; in the world she remembers, magic was only in stories.
Elowen blushes and says it is the only magic she has.
They stand at the edge of the square and look into the Mouth: dark, cold air breathing out.
Elowen says she has the cheapest room at the Brass Kettle, under the eaves, for three nights.
They part at midday; Elowen goes to buy chalk and candles, and they agree to meet at supper.
Nala climbs back up Ladder Lane alone, getting lost once and asking the way.
In room 7 she sits on the bed and unfolds the map: corridors, stairs, careful labels.
She lies back and lets herself be frightened for a while, and then curious.
She spends the afternoon learning her gear: lighting the tin lamp, coiling and knotting rope.
In the evening Wren knocks on door 7 and asks if she is coming down to the Brass Kettle.
The Brass Kettle on Coppergate is cheap, loud and warm, full of delvers.
Elowen is already there at a corner table, and waves, relieved.
Nala introduces Wren and Elowen; Wren grins and makes room on the bench.
Supper is four pennies: stew, bread and small beer. Nala pays and has three pennies left.
Wren tells delving stories; Elowen hangs on every word; Nala laughs more than she expected.

event: Wren counts the table on her fingers: two coppers and one iron makes three.
Wren says, half joking, that three is a party, and looks at them both.
Elowen goes pink and says she would like that, if Nala would.
Nala says she would, and Wren slaps the table, and they agree to talk about it tomorrow.
Nala notices she likes looking at them both: Wren's grin, Elowen's green eyes.
She feels it as plainly in this body as she ever did as Alan, and keeps it to herself.
Elowen walks up to her room under the eaves; Wren and Nala climb Ladder Lane together.

event: She lies down in the narrow bed with the copper token still around her neck.
Through the wall and across the landing she hears Wren humming.
She falls asleep wondering what the Deep will be like, and not how she will get home.
A day in Emberdeep ends.
